240	    def calculate_metrics(self) -> PerformanceMetrics:

253	        by_reflex = self._calculate_by_reflex(recs, outcomes)
254	        trend = self._calculate_trend(outcomes)
255	
256	        return PerformanceMetrics(

258	            outcomes_tracked=tracked,

267	    def _calculate_by_prototype(
268	        self, recs: List[dict], outcomes: List[dict]
269	    ) -> Dict[str, Dict]:
270	        """Calculate metrics by prototype."""
271	        by_proto = {}
272	
273	        for rec in recs:
274	            proto = rec["prototype_matched"]
275	            if proto not in by_proto:
276	                by_proto[proto] = {"total": 0, "tracked": 0, "success": 0}
277	            by_proto[proto]["total"] += 1
278	
279	        rec_map = {r["id"]: r for r in recs}
280	        for outcome in outcomes:
281	            rec = rec_map.get(outcome["recommendation_id"])
282	            if rec:
283	                proto = rec["prototype_matched"]
284	                by_proto[proto]["tracked"] += 1
285	                if outcome.get("success"):
286	                    by_proto[proto]["success"] += 1
287	
288	        for stats in by_proto.values():
289	            if stats["tracked"] > 0:
290	                stats["success_rate"] = round(stats["success"] / stats["tracked"], 2)
291	            else:
292	                stats["success_rate"] = None
293	
294	        return by_proto

29	    def __init__(self, data_dir: Optional[Path] = None):
30	        if data_dir is None:

51	        """Add a new prototype to the library."""
52	        existing_ids = {p.id for p in self._prototypes}
53	        if prototype.id in existing_ids:
54	            raise ValueError(f"Prototype {prototype.id} already exists")
55	        self._prototypes.append(prototype)
56	        self._save_prototypes()
57	        return prototype.id

60	        """Get prototype by ID."""
61	        for p in self._prototypes:
62	            if p.id == prototype_id:
63	                return p
64	        return None

67	        """List all prototypes, optionally filtered by category."""
68	        if category is None:
69	            return self._prototypes.copy()
70	        return [p for p in self._prototypes if p.category == category]

72	    def match(self, situation: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[PrototypeMatch]:
73	        """
74	        Match situation to prototypes using RPD model.
75	
76	        Args:
77	            situation: Dict describing the situation (free-form keys)
78	
79	        Returns:
80	            Ranked list of prototype matches above threshold.
81	        """
82	        situation_text = self._situation_to_text(situation)
83	        matches = []
84	
85	        for proto in self._prototypes:
86	            score, matched, missing = self._calculate_match_score(situation_text, proto)
87	            if score >= self.MATCH_THRESHOLD:
88	                matches.append(PrototypeMatch(
89	                    prototype_id=proto.id,
90	                    prototype_name=proto.name,
91	                    confidence=round(score, 2),
92	                    matched_cues=matched,
93	                    missing_must_have=missing,
94	                    expert_response=proto.expert_response,
95	                    source=proto.source,

103	        parts = []

105	            if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
106	                parts.append(f"{key}: {', '.join(str(v) for v in value)}")
107	            elif isinstance(value, dict):
108	                parts.append(f"{key}: {json.dumps(value)}")

3	**Purpose:** Foundation knowledge for /stage0 hypothesis generation. Injected into Step 5 + Step 6 agent prompts. Single source of truth — do NOT duplicate into agent files.

9	## Core Principle
10	
11	Money = record of transactional friction resolved. The 7 flow types below classify HOW friction is monetized. The 5 compound engines classify WHAT makes revenue grow without proportional effort. The 4 founder strengths classify WHO is best positioned for each.
12	
13	**Anti-bias rule (enforced in Step 5):** Every /stage0 run MUST produce hypotheses spanning ≥2 distinct money-flow types. If all 5 hypotheses share the same type → reject batch, regenerate.

17	## 7 Money-Flow Types (ranked by compound potential)
18	
19	### Type 1 — Labor
20	- **Mechanism:** Sell personal time directly. Revenue = hours × rate.
21	- **Compound potential:** 0% (ceiling = 24hrs/day × your rate)
22	- **Typical range:** $30-300/hr depending on skill scarcity
23	- **Example:** Freelance developer, consultant, designer
24	- **Routing:** Only recommend when founder has no leverage asset yet AND wants near-zero capital start. Always paired with stair-step path to #2 or #3.
25	- **Kill signal:** Still doing all delivery at month 12 → freelancer trap confirmed
26	
27	### Type 2 — Service-at-scale
28	- **Mechanism:** Sell TEAM time. Revenue = headcount × per-person output × margin. Operator manages, does not deliver.
29	- **Compound potential:** Linear with team size; accelerates when distribution lock-in achieved
30	- **Typical range:** $5K-$500K/mo depending on team size and margin
31	- **Example:** VA operations, MCN, content agency, outsourced dev shop, cleaning franchise network
32	- **Routing:** Operations Master primary path. Relationship Master secondary.
33	- **Labor arbitrage pattern lives here** — hire where cost is low, sell where price is high
34	- **Kill signal:** Operator still doing delivery → not at-scale yet; VA turnover >40%/quarter → management failure
35	
36	### Type 3 — Product margin
37	- **Mechanism:** Sell units (physical or digital) at markup. Revenue = units × (price - COGS).
38	- **Compound potential:** Exponential if LTV > CAC; SaaS compounds via churn inversion
39	- **Typical range:** $1K-$10M+/mo; power-law distribution (most products $0, top 1% = all value)
40	- **Example:** E-commerce, SaaS, digital product, physical good with brand
41	- **Routing:** Skills Master (product builders), Market Master (inventory traders)
42	- **CURRENT /stage0 DEFAULT BIAS** — Step 5 must actively resist defaulting here
43	- **Kill signal:** COGS >80% of price with no moat → commodity trap
44	
45	### Type 4 — Rent
46	- **Mechanism:** Charge for access to an asset you own. Revenue = access_fee × users.
47	- **Compound potential:** Near-infinite if asset maintained and demand grows; zero marginal cost per user
48	- **Typical range:** $500/mo (small niche tool) to $10M+/mo (real estate portfolio, dominant platform)
49	- **Example:** Real estate rent, SaaS seat licenses, domain parking, API access, marketplace listing fee
50	- **Routing:** Operations Master (managing assets), Market Master (buying undervalued assets)
51	- **Kill signal:** Asset degrades faster than rent revenue → net negative; platform revoke = total loss
52	
53	### Type 5 — Arbitrage
54	- **Mechanism:** Capture spread between two inefficient markets. Revenue = (sell_price - buy_price) × volume.
55	- **Compound potential:** Exponential until spread closes; time-sensitive (moat = discovery speed + execution)
56	- **Typical range:** $2K-$500K/mo; collapses when market discovers the spread
57	- **Example:** Geographic price arbitrage (1688→Amazon), information arbitrage (knowing before market), currency/commodity spread
58	- **Routing:** Market Master primary. Skills Master with technical arbitrage (data API price gaps).
59	- **HIGHEST potential for VN-native + EN-intermediate + tech stack** — geographic arbitrage structural advantage
60	- **Kill signal:** Spread < 30% → margin erosion; competing arbitrageurs visible in same channel
61	
62	### Type 6 — Float
63	- **Mechanism:** Hold other people's money before paying it out. Revenue = interest/yield on float + float timing advantage.
64	- **Compound potential:** Silent and powerful; compounding on principal × time
65	- **Typical range:** $1K-$100M+/mo (insurance float is the ultimate expression)
66	- **Example:** Insurance premiums, trade finance, escrow services, pre-payment models, subscription upfront
67	- **Routing:** Relationship Master (trust required); requires regulatory compliance in most jurisdictions
68	- **Kill signal:** Regulatory clampdown on unlicensed float; counterparty default risk
69	
70	### Type 7 — Capital gains
71	- **Mechanism:** Buy asset cheap, sell high. Revenue = (exit_price - entry_price) on each transaction.
72	- **Compound potential:** Power-law; rare home runs fund many losses; requires judgment AND capital
73	- **Typical range:** $0 (most attempts) to $10M+ per exit; requires multi-year horizon
74	- **Example:** Domain flipping, business acquisition + exit, real estate appreciation, equity investments
75	- **Routing:** Market Master (timing), Relationship Master (deal access), Operations Master (value-add operators)
76	- **Kill signal:** No exit market → asset illiquid; bought at peak, no value-add lever
77

80	## 5 Compound Engines (what actually generates asymmetric wealth)
81	
82	### Engine 1 — Code
83	- **Description:** Software written once, deployed to N users with near-zero marginal cost.
84	- **Time to 10x revenue:** 18-36 months (after product-market fit)
85	- **Capital required:** $500-$50K (build cost) + infrastructure
86	- **Example operators:** Bannerbear ($50K+/mo, Jules Ugokwe), Plausible Analytics ($1M+/ARR), Tony Dinh (~$50K/mo Xnapper)
87	- **Requires:** Technical skill or outsourced dev
88	- **Breaks when:** Platform dependency (API changes), security breach, copycat with VC funding
89	
90	### Engine 2 — Data
91	- **Description:** Every use of data makes the asset more valuable; others can't replicate without the same inputs.
92	- **Time to 10x revenue:** 36-60 months
93	- **Capital required:** High ($10K-$1M for proprietary data collection)
94	- **Example operators:** Bloomberg Terminal ($6B/yr), Panjiva (acquired by S&P for $550M), Masothue.com (VN business registry scraper)
95	- **Requires:** Unique access or systematic collection over time; analysis capability
96	- **Breaks when:** Data source opens up (becomes free), regulation blocks collection
97	
98	### Engine 3 — Audience
99	- **Description:** Each follower/subscriber = distribution asset; future products flow through for near-zero CAC.
100	- **Time to 10x revenue:** 24-48 months
101	- **Capital required:** $0-$5K (time-heavy)
102	- **Example operators:** Pieter Levels (500K+ Twitter, funds product launches), Justin Welsh ($5M+/yr via newsletter), Codie Sanchez (2M+ subscribers, 8-figure portfolio access)

107	- **Description:** Trust compounds; you charge more over time for same service; waiting list emerges.

109	- **Capital required:** $0 (time-heavy)

111	- **Requires:** Domain expertise + verifiable track record; client results documented

119	- **Requires:** Early mover OR capital to buy position OR Operations Master execution
120	- **Breaks when:** Platform changes ranking algo; new channel emerges and audience migrates

127	- **Core strength:** Technical depth — can build things others can't
128	- **Signal keywords:** software engineer, developer, designer, math, engineering, technical, "I built", code, algorithm
